nodes.title: Branch schedule (same numbers as the stages)
STEP A — DISCOVER

properties.text:
## Step A — discover

Cheap candidates from consecutive seeds: `origin`, `origin+1`, `origin+2`, …
Only `A` steps are spent per candidate, so this is where to be generous.

**How many samples?** — your main speed dial. Cost is linear. Many cheap
candidates early and few expensive ones late is the entire idea.

**There is no theta here.** Step A has no parent to move away from — it is
discovering, not varying. That asymmetry is real, not an oversight.

### Choosing
Click a tile to see it large, or use ◀ Prev / Next ▶. The buttons only move the
`index` widget, so choosing is an ordinary graph edit — **re-queue when you have
picked**.

The readout appends `(re-queue)` when your cursor has moved off the candidate
that actually ran, so a stale selection is never mistaken for a live one.

The seed it reports *is* that candidate's identity: `origin_seed + index`.

nodes.title: theta and spread

properties.text:
## theta vs spread — the two dials people confuse

**theta = how far from the parent.** The only magnitude control.

| theta | |
|---|---|
| `0` | an **exact** reproduction of the parent's continuation — the control |
| `10–45` | the useful working range |
| `90` | a fresh direction at the same noise level |

theta is literally the angle: `cos_sim(parent, child) = cos(theta)`, accurate to
a fraction of a degree. Past 90 the children keep moving away from the parent
while collapsing back *together*, so variety stops improving.

**spread = how widely the children fan out** around that distance. `0–90`,
default `90`. Without it, how different the children are from *each other* was
locked to how far they are from the *parent* — "go somewhere new but keep this
family tight" was inexpressible.

| spread → | 0 | 30 | 45 | 60 | 90 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| theta 25 | 0.0 | 17.2 | 24.4 | 30.0 | 34.8 |
| theta 45 | 0.0 | 29.0 | 41.4 | 51.3 | 60.0 |
| theta 60 | 0.0 | 35.7 | 51.3 | 64.1 | 75.5 |

*(degrees between siblings)*

### Why theta = 0 makes spread do nothing
The parent is the north pole. **theta is the latitude line** every child stands
on; **spread is how far apart they are spaced along it.** At theta 0 that circle
has shrunk to the pole — six people spaced maximally around a zero-radius circle
all stand on the same spot.

It is the triangle inequality, not a quirk. It is also *required*: theta 0 being
an exact reproduction is the baseline that lets you say "this branch is identical
to not branching".

**Keep the parent direction?** — makes child 1 the parent's exact continuation
and the rest variations around it. A single theta can't give you both, since
every child sits the same distance away; this lets one child sit at zero.

nodes.title: Generative Trajectory Explorer

properties.text:
# Generative Trajectory Explorer

A normal generation runs from pure noise to a finished image in one go — you pay
full price before knowing whether the seed was any good.

This one **stops part-way, lets you look, and continues only what you picked**,
branching into variations at each stop. You pay full price only for the branches
you keep.

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **STEP A** | DISCOVER | `0 → A` · many seeds, cheap. Pick a direction. |
| **STEP B** | BRANCH | `A → B` · vary the one you picked. Pick again. |
| **STEP C** | BRANCH | `B → C` · vary again, more finely. Pick again. |
| **FINAL** | | `C → end` · finish the one you chose. |

The unit of work is **a partial latent plus the noise level it sits at**.
A latent without its sigma is meaningless — that idea is why everything here
is built the way it is.

### Every control answers exactly one question

| question | control |
|---|---|
| where do I stop? | **Checkpoint A / B / C** |
| how far do I move? | **theta** — the only magnitude dial |
| which way do I move? | **variation seed** — direction only, no magnitude |
| how do siblings fan out? | **spread** — shares out what theta allocated |

None of them answers two. If you are reaching for the wrong dial, it is almost
always theta vs spread — see the Step B note.

nodes.title: How to read the controls

properties.text:
## Global controls

**Total Steps** — how long the full schedule is. Everything else is measured
against it. There is ONE schedule and each stage takes an absolute slice, so
changing this moves everything consistently. Nothing to rewire.

**Checkpoint A / B / C** — the absolute steps where the run stops.
Must increase: `0 < A < B < C < Total`.

> **Pick these by noise level, not step number.** The same step means wildly
> different things under different schedulers. Read *Noise left at each step*
> (bottom of the graph) and put checkpoints where there is still something to
> work with. At 20 steps on `kl_optimal`:
>
> | step | noise left | |
> |---|---|---|
> | 5 | 65% | still a rough direction |
> | 10 | 39% | composition committing |
> | 15 | 17% | layout fixed, treatment open |

Branch **too late** and there is nothing left to vary. Branch **too early** and
you are not varying your choice, you are re-rolling it.

**Width / Height** — round to a multiple of **16** on Flux2 (8 on SD1.5).
Anything else is silently rounded down at decode (910 comes back as 896).

**Sampler: `euler`. Do not change.** Splitting a trajectory only works for a
sampler whose next step depends on `(x, sigma)` alone. `dpmpp_2m` carries
derivative history and degrades; `dpmpp_2m_sde` injects its own noise and breaks.

**Scheduler: `kl_optimal`** on Flux2/krea2. `karras` is built for models whose
sigma runs 14.6 → 0 and collapses a flow schedule into its first few steps —
97% of the image done by step 5, nothing left to branch on.

**Use negative prompt?** — ON for SD1.5/SDXL (CFG does real work). OFF for
Flux/krea2: guidance is distilled in, CFG on top is wrong, and off is faster.

**Flux guidance** — flux2 only, default 3.5. Does nothing on krea2 / SD1.5 /
SDXL; those models never read it. Harmless to leave wired.

nodes.title: Reading a run  ·  troubleshooting

properties.text:
## What the console tells you

```
Resume Step: latent resumes at step 5     ← where this stage began
Stamp Step: latent is at step 10          ← where it ended
Candidate Select: 2/20  seed 701          ← which one you kept
Noise Rotate: 15 descendant(s) at
             theta=25deg from seed 500
```

If these disagree with your checkpoint controls, **trust the console** — it is
reporting the latent, and the latent is what gets sampled.

## When it misbehaves

**Nothing is changing.**
theta too low — or you branched too late and there is no noise left to vary.
Check the noise table.

**It changed completely / went off-prompt.**
theta too high for that depth. Lower it, or branch deeper.

**The children are all identical.**
`spread = 0`, or `theta = 0`. You are paying N renders for one image.

**Results look soft, or cracked and over-worked.**
The noise level and the step number disagree. Usually the wrong scheduler
(`karras` on a flow model), or a variation seed colliding with the origin seed.

## Quick recipes

| want | settings |
|---|---|
| lots of options, cheap | Total 20, A 5, samples 20+ |
| nearby versions of this | theta 15–25, spread 90, keep_parent ON |
| same layout, new treatment | branch at C, theta 30–45, spread 90 |
| somewhere new, tight family | theta 45, spread 20–30 |
